label: Figure 20.10: The long-run Phillips curve
alt: Three short-run Phillips curves SRPC1, SRPC2 and SRPC3 and a vertical LRPC at the natural rate of unemployment, 5%. The economy moves A(5%, 3%) to B(3%, 7%) to C(5%, 7%) to D(3%, 11%) to E(5%, 11%).
caption: Start at A on SRPC<sub>1</sub>: unemployment is at the natural rate of 5% and inflation is 3%. Expansionary policy moves the economy along SRPC<sub>1</sub> to B (3% unemployment, 7% inflation). When workers see through the money illusion and expect higher inflation, the curve shifts up to SRPC<sub>2</sub> and unemployment returns to 5% at C (7% inflation). Repeating the policy gives D (3%, 11%) and then E (5%, 11%) on SRPC<sub>3</sub>. Joining A, C and E gives the vertical long-run Phillips curve (LRPC) at the natural rate: no long-run trade-off.
